title: Count of smaller numbers after self
statement: For each element, count the elements to its right that are strictly smaller.
hints: Scan from the right, keeping a structure of values seen so far; ask "how many are < x?"
Values up to 10⁹: compress them to ranks 1..n first.

solution.explanation: Scanning right to left turns "elements after me" into "elements already inserted". A Fenwick tree over compressed ranks counts how many inserted values are below x. Coordinate compression (sort the distinct values, map to 1..m) is what makes value-indexed structures possible when values are huge. Merge sort with inversion counting is the alternative, also O(n log n).
solution.python:
def count_smaller(nums):
    vals = sorted(set(nums)); rank = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(vals)}; n = len(vals); bit = [0] * (n + 1); out = []
    for x in reversed(nums):
        i = rank[x] - 1; s = 0
        while i > 0: s += bit[i]; i -= i & -i
        out.append(s); i = rank[x]
        while i <= n: bit[i] += 1; i += i & -i
    return out[::-1]
